title: Merz Rallies CDU With 'Germany Has the Strength for a New Beginning' as Succession Talk Mounts
detail: Chancellor Friedrich Merz delivered a major internal CDU address on May 28, 2026, vowing to press ahead with his reform agenda and declaring 'Germany has the strength for a new beginning' — a direct attempt to silence growing party unrest. The speech followed reporting by German tabloid Bild that senior CDU members were informally discussing potential successors as Merz's approval rating hovered at approximately 16%, one of the lowest levels for a sitting German chancellor in modern polling records. Bild named three CDU state leaders as potential replacements: NRW Minister-President Hendrik Wüst, Hesse Minister-President Boris Rhein, and Saxony's Michael Kretschmer. Bloomberg reported that Merz aimed to 'shut down party unrest with a vow to revive Germany.' In the address, Merz argued that internal CDU divisions were a strategic gift to the AfD — then polling at 28% — and pledged to accelerate the coalition's reform roadmap ahead of the July parliamentary recess. He focused on corporate tax relief, energy cost reduction for industrial firms, and streamlining administrative burdens on Germany's Mittelstand. All three potential CDU successors declined public comment on the speculation. The episode underscored the structural pressures facing Merz: AfD at record polling highs, SPD coalition partner unpopular, reform delivery behind schedule, and US-Germany relations strained by Trump's Ramstein troop withdrawal order.

media.caption: Bloomberg: Merz aims to shut down CDU party unrest with vow to revive Germany
